clue.text: English money for English train

parts.note: E again, the usual abbreviation for English
a ducat is an old gold coin used across Europe
E again, the usual abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone swaps English currency for an English rail ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a noun (a railway train) but works as a verb meaning to teach.
explanation.definitionFit: To train someone is to teach and instruct them, a close synonym of schooling them.

clue.text: Old MP said to have audience of 550, formerly (with 22) adapted by 16 6 10

indicators.note: words spoken to an audience are heard, so the name is taken by its sound

parts.note: Tam Dalyell, long-serving Labour MP, whose surname is pronounced 'dee-ell'

explanation.surface: A veteran politician is said to have addressed a crowd of 550 in times gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scottish name is said 'dee-ell', like Dalyell, and also like the letters DL, which is 550 in Roman numerals, the 'formerly' numbering. With 22 it makes Dalziel and Pascoe, Reginald Hill's detectives, adapted for television by Alan Plater.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalziel is the senior detective of Reginald Hill's novels, whose television series was adapted by the playwright of the theme.

clue.text: Leader of cathedral? Not yet, as a rule …

definitions.meaning: a cathedral clergyman ranking below the dean, who leads the chapter, so not yet its head
a principle or general law, as in the rules of a church or of good taste

explanation.surface: A clergyman is told he is not yet in charge of the cathedral, as is usual.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a member of a cathedral chapter under the dean, and the word also means an accepted rule or law.

clue.text: … stretch done by prisoner must intervene

parts.note: time is what a convict has done, as in 'doing time'
a lag is a slang word for a convict, usually an old lag

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a waiting period must pass, like a sentence served.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 3: a canon must wait some time before he becomes dean. 'Done by' looks like one phrase, but 'by' only joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A time lag is an interval or delay, a stretch of time between cause and effect.

clue.text: Weirdos' chance to entertain Bo Derek initially

definitions.note: the clue's plural possessive; the answer is the plain plural, the 's acting as a link

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to hold them within, so the chance word holds the other letters

parts.note: odds are the chances of something happening
taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the following name

explanation.surface: Strange people get an opportunity to host the film actress Bo Derek.
explanation.walkthrough: The actress's full name looks like one unit, but it gives two pieces: her first name whole, and only the initial of her surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddbods is British slang for eccentric or peculiar people, the same as weirdos.

clue.text: Non-resident student, expert on love year in, year out

indicators.note: the first year goes in, so it sits inside the word for an expert

parts.note: a dab, or dab hand, is an expert
Y again, the second year, placed outside at the end
love means nil in tennis, so it gives O
Y again, the second year, placed outside at the end

explanation.surface: A pupil who lives out is an authority on romance, year after year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Year in, year out' looks like the idiom for constantly, but one Y goes inside DAB and the other goes at the end, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: At a boarding school, a day boy is a pupil who attends lessons but lives at home rather than boarding.

clue.text: Live desire for 16 6 10's work

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
longing means strong desire

explanation.surface: A playwright's work is about a desire for life.
explanation.walkthrough: Belonging is a play by Alan Plater, the playwright behind the cross-referenced lights.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging is the title of one of the playwright's plays, so it is an example of his work.

clue.text: Serious wound for the military establishment?

definitions.meaning: a deep gash or severe laceration, the sense of an injury that goes far into the flesh
the British Army barracks at ... in Surrey, notorious for deaths of recruits there

explanation.surface: A grave injury is asked about as if it were the armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: Deepcut is an army training barracks in Surrey; 'establishment' also hints at the military in general.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep cut is a serious gash, and Deepcut is a well-known British Army base.

clue.text: It was closed by 16 6 10, producing a dolorous echo

indicators.note: producing suggests the letters are worked up into something new, an arrangement

explanation.surface: A door shut by the playwright makes a mournful reverberation.
explanation.walkthrough: Close the Coalhouse Door is a play by Alan Plater; 'producing' asks for the letters of A DOLOROUS ECHO to be rearranged. A coalhouse is a shed for storing coal.
explanation.definitionFit: The play title Close the Coalhouse Door means this door was, in effect, closed by its author.

clue.text: Man from New Zealand

indicators.note: from tells us to take the answer out of the following words, here a run inside the country's name

explanation.surface: A fellow comes from New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan is a man's first name, so it stands for a man.

clue.text: "Music", which is derived from the bloody Muse

indicators.note: something derived from these words is made by reworking their letters into another order

explanation.surface: Music is said to come from a cursed goddess of inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' is a link here. The Moody Blues are a British rock band, so they stand for music.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moody Blues are an English rock group, so the name stands for a kind of music.

clue.text: Snicket walker on way back takes in pub

indicators.note: takes in means the reversed word holds the pub inside it
on the way back means the walker word is read backwards

parts.note: a leg is what one walks on
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A man on a footpath heading home calls in at a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Snicket and ginnel are both northern English dialect words for a narrow passage between houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginnel is a northern English dialect synonym for a snicket, a narrow alley or passageway.

clue.text: Showing some knickers in Cornish resort to appear attractive

indicators.note: in puts part of the underwear word inside the town's name

parts.note: Looe is a seaside town in Cornwall, south-west England

indicators.note: some means only part of the word knickers is used

explanation.surface: Displaying underwear at a seaside resort to look good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showing' is a link word. Looe is a fishing town and holiday resort on the south coast of Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: To look nice is to be attractive in appearance, an idiomatic phrase for appearing pleasing.

clue.text: The Ron Duke?

parts.note: the Iron Duke was the victor of Waterloo; knock the first letter off Iron to get Ron, do the same to the general's title, and you reach a jazz bandleader also known as Duke

explanation.surface: A nickname for some aristocrat called Ron.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iron Duke is the famous nickname of the general who won Waterloo. Remove the opening letter of his title, as Ron is Iron less its I, and you get the American jazz bandleader Duke.
explanation.definitionFit: Duke Ellington's name is Wellington less its first letter, as Ron is Iron less its first letter.

clue.text: Supplier of water for Irish capital on hill

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone provides water to the Irish capital from a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish capital' suggests Dublin, but 'Irish' gives IR and 'capital' is Riga.
explanation.definitionFit: An irrigator is a person or device that supplies water to land or crops.

clue.text: Arrival of Lord John at hospital

parts.note: John Birt, later Lord Birt, was Director-General of the BBC
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A peer named John turns up at the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link word; John Birt ran the BBC in the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: A birth is the arrival of a baby, so arrival is a fair stand-in for it.

clue.text: Olympic figure (Berlin's and period omitted), it is the House of Commons — nothing the matter with 16 6 10's work

indicators.note: omitted means these pieces are left out of the name of the sporting official

parts.note: Avery Brundage was president of the International Olympic Committee
in Berlin, 'and' is the German und
an age is a period of time
taken as written, the two words joined
H is the abbreviation for House
C is the abbreviation for Commons
nothing is zero, which looks like O
'what's up?' asks what the matter is, so up means the matter

explanation.surface: An Olympic official, minus German and an era, says Parliament is in good shape for the playwright's drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking UND and AGE out of AVERY BRUNDAGE leaves AVERY BR. Then come IT IS, H of C (House of Commons), O and UP. Alan Plater adapted Chris Mullin's novel A Very British Coup for television.
explanation.definitionFit: A Very British Coup is the television serial Alan Plater wrote from Chris Mullin's novel, so it counts as his work.

clue.text: House companion in Austria

definitions.note: a phrase pointing to a place in Austria, not a noun itself

parts.note: a villa is a large house
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Someone sharing a house in Austria.
explanation.walkthrough: Villach is a town in southern Austria, in Carinthia.
explanation.definitionFit: Villach is a town in the Carinthia region of southern Austria, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: Barbarian to go short, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A barbarian is unhappy at having to go without.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ostrogoths were a Germanic people who invaded the Roman Empire, the classic barbarians.

clue.text: Make further inroads into Green territory

indicators.note: into points inside the following words, where the answer runs across them

explanation.surface: Push deeper into environmentalist strongholds.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-enter is to go in again, to make a further incursion into a place.

clue.text: Causes of circulation predicated of money, they say

indicators.note: they say means we go by the sound of a word, not its spelling

parts.note: the saying 'money talks' predicates talking of money

explanation.surface: The forces of circulation are attributed to money, according to people.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British accent the verb TALKS sounds like the answer. A torque is a twisting force that makes things rotate.
explanation.definitionFit: Torques are twisting forces, the physical causes of rotation or turning motion.

clue.text: The not so old bean, not French, runner

parts.note: pas is French for not
Sebastian Coe is a British Olympic middle-distance runner

explanation.surface: A young chap, not French, goes for a run.
explanation.walkthrough: Pascoe is the younger partner of the older Dalziel in Reginald Hill's novels, so he is the 'not so old bean'; 'bean' is old British slang for a chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Pascoe is the junior, younger detective paired with the older Dalziel, a younger fellow in the partnership.

clue.text: Lazy fellow, a pest, and where, mostly

parts.note: a slug is a garden pest

indicators.note: mostly means the word for the pest's home loses its end

parts.note: the garden is where a slug lives

explanation.surface: An idle man is a nuisance, and so is where he hangs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where' works only through the pest: the garden is where slugs live. 'Mostly' trims the last two letters of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sluggard is a habitually lazy, idle person.

clue.text: See 29
Good place for baby with loop

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means good
a cot is a baby's bed

explanation.surface: A good place to put a baby with a ring of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A picot is a small decorative loop of thread on the edge of lace or ribbon.

clue.text: Throw a punch? Don't do it yet!

definitions.meaning: to hit someone, read literally, as a clout is a blow
from the proverb 'Ne'er ... till May be out', telling you not to shed winter clothes too early

explanation.surface: Someone thinking of hitting out is told to wait.
explanation.walkthrough: In the old proverb, a clout is a piece of clothing; the advice is to keep warm clothes on until May is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally the phrase means landing a blow, while the proverb uses it for taking off clothes too soon.

clue.text: See 17
Don't talk audibly before time to novel heroine

parts.note: sh is the word used to tell someone to be quiet

indicators.note: audibly means the next word is taken by how it sounds, not how it is spelt

parts.note: early means before the expected time

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stay quiet ahead of the hour for a heroine of a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: SH followed by a word that sounds like EARLY gives the name. Shirley is the heroine of Charlotte Brontë's novel Shirley.
explanation.definitionFit: Shirley is the title heroine of Charlotte Brontë's 1849 novel, so she is a heroine of a novel.

clue.text: Now 16 6 10's command: treat him with beer and spirit

indicators.note: to treat something is to process or work on it, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man is offered beer and spirits as a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Plater was made a CBE, Commander of the Order of the British Empire, so this is now his command. Himbeergeist, a German raspberry spirit, hides in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: As a Commander of its Order, the playwright now holds a command in this imperial honours order.
